note: The information register (task T42, session arena/d26f42db-zone2). Three sections. `answered` = a question an official source settles, with the verbatim answer and its link. `open` = a question nothing in the repository can answer; every row states what is already known, what is missing, and the concrete action that would close it. `inventory` = what the project already holds, each item with the source that establishes it. An open row has an empty `answer` on purpose: nothing is inferred to fill it. This register extends, and does not replace, the canonical Q-01..Q-16 at pages/questions.html.

sections.answered: Settled by an official source. The `answer` field quotes or restates only what the linked page says.
sections.open: Not answerable from anything in this repository. `answer` is blank by design.
sections.inventory: What the project already has, with the source that establishes it.

answered.question: What disclosure sentence must appear on the site?
answered.answer: “As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.”, stated clearly and prominently, or any substantially similar statement previously allowed under the Agreement.
answered.consequence: Measured at build time on every rebuild: the sentence is present on every page in the published tree. The live count is on the repository review page — it is not typed here, because five sessions were merging pages into this tree concurrently and a typed count goes stale.

answered.question: May the site publish an earnings estimate or a traffic projection?
answered.answer: No. “We do not make any representation, warranty, or covenant regarding the amount of traffic or commission income you can expect at any time in connection with the Associates Program.”
answered.consequence: No page here may forecast revenue. Every proposal on this board is costed in effort, never in money.

answered.question: Can the site show product prices today?
answered.answer: Only if Amazon serves the link containing the price, or the price comes from Creators API or PA API. Neither holds today.
answered.consequence: Every price cell stays blank. This is a rule, not a gap.

answered.question: Can the site show star ratings or customer reviews?
answered.answer: Not unless obtained through Creators API or PA API.
answered.consequence: No rating appears anywhere in the tree, and none may be added.

answered.question: May the site have price tracking or price alerts?
answered.answer: “Unless otherwise agreed by Amazon, your Site must not have price tracking and/or price alerting functionality.”
answered.consequence: Module M-03 as written in the brief is out of scope unless Amazon agrees in writing.

answered.question: What commission rate applies to these products?
answered.answer: Table 1 lists “Physical Books, Kitchen, Automotive” at 4.50%. All Other Categories is 4.00%.
answered.consequence: The three resolved destinations all sit in the Air Fryers browse node, but the band that applies to a specific product is Amazon's to assign, not this project's. Recorded as unconfirmed for planning.

answered.question: What does Amazon require before it will even review an application?
answered.answer: At least three qualifying sales within the first 180 days; personal orders do not qualify. Sites must have robust original content — “a good rule of thumb is at least 10 posts” — be recent (generally within the last 60 days), publicly available, and owned by the applicant.
answered.consequence: The site cannot be approved before it has produced sales, and cannot earn before it is approved. That loop is the project's central constraint and it is not technical.

answered.question: What does Amazon say separates a good affiliate site from a rejected one?
answered.answer: A site that “adds value to the customer by giving them insight on a subject or product they might not get easily”, and where “successful sites will give the customer a unique experience or insight that is not available anywhere else.”
answered.consequence: This is the standard the redesign pack is written against. It is also, indirectly, the answer to the “reads like AI slop” complaint: insight the reader cannot get elsewhere is the bar.

answered.question: Are the supplied short codes valid ASINs?
answered.answer: No. Amazon defines the ASIN as “the 10-digit code that Amazon uses to denote specific products”; all three supplied codes are 9 characters. A control run this session confirms the short-link service refuses a valid 10-character ASIN with the same 404 it returns for an unknown code, so the service does not accept ASINs at all.
answered.consequence: The codes are opaque short-link identifiers. Nothing about a product can be inferred from them; only the page each one resolves to is evidence.

answered.question: Can the links as supplied earn a commission?
answered.answer: Not reliably. Every link must carry the assigned Associates ID as a URL parameter; all three resolved URLs were observed without one, and no Associates ID exists in the repository.
answered.consequence: Revenue is blocked by one missing identifier, not by any technical gap.

answered.question: Is organic search traffic allowed for an affiliate site?
answered.answer: Yes, “so long as you comply with the Agreement and those paid or unpaid search results send users to your site and not directly, or indirectly via a Redirecting Link, to an Amazon Site.”
answered.consequence: The traffic plan is legitimate. It must land on this site first.

answered.question: Is generating many pages with an AI tool a policy violation?
answered.answer: It is a spam-policy violation when the pages are generated “for the primary purpose of manipulating search rankings and not helping users”; Google's first listed example is “using generative AI tools or other similar tools to generate many pages without adding value for users”.
answered.consequence: The tool is not the problem. Volume without value is.

answered.question: Must generated content be checked by a person before publishing?
answered.answer: “It is critical to manually factcheck and review all AI-generated content for accuracy and trustworthiness before publishing.” The same review applies to titles, meta descriptions, structured data and image alt text.
answered.consequence: Proposal P-04 exists because of this sentence.

answered.question: May Program Content be used to build or train machine-learning models?
answered.answer: Not without Amazon's express prior written approval: “You will not, without our express prior written approval, use, or allow any third party to use, any Special Links or Program Content to develop machine learning models or related technology.”
answered.consequence: The brief asks for an AI platform built on Program Content. That needs written permission before it is built, not after. Flagged as IR-05.

answered.question: Is having affiliate links on a page itself a problem for Google?
answered.answer: No. “It's not a violation of our policies to have such links as long as they are qualified with a rel="nofollow" or rel="sponsored" attribute value to the <a> tag.”
answered.consequence: The published tree already qualifies its outbound affiliate anchors; the existing gates check this on every build.

open.question: What is the single public address and canonical home of this project?
open.have: The live site is at https://kanlerxz87-cyber.github.io/Zone2/ and 116 HTML pages are published across 11 top-level namespaces, each with its own index and navigation.
open.missing: Which one is the site. Nothing in the repository records a decision.
open.how_to_find: Owner picks one path as the public home. Everything else is either moved under it or labelled archive. Then one canonical host is written into every page.

open.question: What is the site called?
open.have: Six different names are in use across the namespaces, measured from each page's <title> on 2026-11-15: Zone2, Counter Notes, Zone2 decisions, Zone2 Revalidation, Zone2 — Amazon Affiliate Intelligence Dashboard, Northstar · Affiliate Intelligence.
open.missing: Which one the owner wants. Also whether the name is available as a domain and whether it is free of Amazon marks, which the Trademark Guidelines require.
open.how_to_find: Owner chooses a name; agent checks the chosen string against the Amazon mark list and domain availability.

open.question: Is the objective income, or a demonstrator?
open.have: The brief asks for a revenue-maximising automation platform. The repository as built is a source-governed research and verification tree with no monetised link on it.
open.missing: Which of the two the owner actually wants next. They pull in opposite directions: a demonstrator can publish more surfaces; an income site must consolidate and needs the Associates account first.
open.how_to_find: Owner states the objective in one sentence.

open.question: Who is the named person responsible for what gets published?
open.have: No page in any namespace names a person. Google lists “stated or implied authorship” as an objective factor in whether a section is considered part of the main site.
open.missing: A name, and that person's agreement to be named.
open.how_to_find: Owner names an editor. If the owner does not want to be named, a publication name plus a contact route is the fallback — weaker, but honest.

open.question: How often is a verified fact re-checked, and by whom?
open.have: Both governing documents carry their own update dates and change without notice; the Operating Agreement currently reads “Updated: October 15, 2025”. Six sessions have re-verified the same three links and reached at least two different readings.
open.missing: A cadence, and an owner for it.
open.how_to_find: Owner sets a cadence (monthly and on every policy-page change is the suggestion). Agent implements it as a dated check on each fact-bearing page.

open.question: Is there a budget for a domain and hosting?
open.have: The Associates application requires that “You must own your website”. The site currently runs on a github.io address under the repository owner's account.
open.missing: Whether the owner will buy a domain, and whether a github.io address satisfies the ownership test — Amazon's published pages do not settle the second point.
open.how_to_find: Owner decides. If a domain is bought, the canonical host changes everywhere in one commit.

open.question: Does anyone connected with this project physically have these three machines?
open.have: Three Amazon listings the supplied links resolve to, and manufacturer specification pages for each. That is all.
open.missing: Any dated record of anyone using any of them. Without it the site cannot make a first-hand claim, and Google's list of what makes an affiliate page good names “original product reviews” and “rigorous testing and ratings”.
open.how_to_find: Owner states yes or no. If yes, a dated test log with photographs is the asset that most differentiates this site from every competitor. If no, the site stays specification-led and says so.

open.question: Should the internal verification surfaces stay public?
open.have: Verification logs, source registers, requirement matrices, flag registers, revalidation sets and two second-opinion dashboards are all published and indexable.
open.missing: Whether that is deliberate. These are working documents — a reader landing on a 976-link integrity check is not a buyer.
open.how_to_find: Owner decides. Suggestion: keep them, move them under one clearly internal path, and exclude them from search.

open.question: Which kitchen is the reader in?
open.have: All three resolved listings are on amazon.com and their breadcrumb reads Home & Kitchen › Kitchen & Dining › Small Appliances › Fryers › Air Fryers. The brief's operator location is Osaka, Japan.
open.missing: Whether the reader is a US household cook on 120 V or a Japanese one on 100 V. Capacity in quarts, temperature in °F and counter depth in inches all assume the first.
open.how_to_find: Owner states the audience. Agent then checks whether the same ASINs are sold on the target marketplace before any article is written.

open.question: Will there be an email list or newsletter?
open.have: Amazon permits Special Links in email and SMS only where the communication is solicited, and makes the sender legally responsible for each one.
open.missing: Whether the owner wants one at all.
open.how_to_find: Owner decides. If yes, it needs a real opt-in and a documented consent record before the first send.

open.question: Has anyone asked Amazon for written permission to use Program Content in machine-learning work?
open.have: The rule requires express prior written approval. No record of a request exists in the repository.
open.missing: Whether a request was made, and the answer if it was.
open.how_to_find: Owner checks sent mail and Associates Central correspondence. If no request was made, the automation scope in the brief cannot proceed as written.
open.priority: P1 — blocks the automation scope of the brief

open.question: What does finished mean for this project?
open.have: 116 pages, 38 flags, 16 open questions, 10 open suggestions, 14 open marketing-board items, 30-odd sessions of work, and no monetised link.
open.missing: A definition of done. Without one, every session adds another surface.
open.how_to_find: Owner writes one sentence: what the site should be able to do in 90 days that it cannot do today.
